scope: Real elevenid-beta Python passport retirement before the single post-deletion Rust deployment; production is outside this operation
shared_service: Beta issuance is one Python service for passport and unrelated issuance routes. Keep unrelated issuance available; the passport writer is the physical-document job and Flow write surface, not the whole container.

required_identity: exact Python issuance container ID, immutable image digest and Compose labels
PostgreSQL container ID, cluster system identifier and database identity
Gateway and Flow container IDs, image digests and passport owner selectors
the protected main source, signed stack manifest and exact Credentials deletion PR head
authority.reject: Ambiguous or changed identity, production labels, an already active unrelated mutation, or a missing protected release blocks the operation

database_enforcement.ownership: Enumerate every live application and migration database role with write or DDL access to guarded objects. Create a trusted guard owner with NOLOGIN and transfer ownership of the issuance_service and flow_service schemas and three fenced tables away from every live app role. Preserve the schema, table, sequence and function privileges needed for unrelated runtime behavior without granting trigger or guarded-object DDL control. No live app role may own, disable, drop, replace, or bypass fence triggers, functions, or state; verify owners, enabled triggers, memberships and effective grants before and after installation.
database_enforcement.migrations: Before installing the fence, prove a trusted migration path for the later official deployment. A separate privileged migration executor, unavailable to live application containers, may change non-guarded schema objects under the beta deployment lock. Any DDL on guarded tables or schemas must preserve the effective fence, revalidate its definitions and grants before applications restart, and leave it installed until the Rust-owner transition. Never grant temporary guarded-object DDL to a live app role or run the existing app-role migration unchanged if ownership would make it fail.
database_enforcement.truncate: Revoke TRUNCATE and ownership-derived TRUNCATE from every live application and migration role on the guarded tables, and install a rejecting TRUNCATE trigger for direct and CASCADE paths. Prove rows cannot be discarded by TRUNCATE after fence installation.
database_enforcement.predicate: Guard the exact physical-document job table and physical-document Flow definitions/instances using both OLD and NEW rows. A write to a definitionless instance is denied only when its structure proves physical-document work; unrelated verification writes remain available. The separate conservative drain selector in passport-beta-cutover-drain-behavior.json still counts every other nonterminal definitionless instance except its exact expired synthetic OID4VP orphan shape; those rows block installation or later receipts without being mislabeled as passport writes. Do not deny unrelated defined Flows merely because context text contains the word passport.
database_enforcement.phase_visibility: The atomic install takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks on all three guarded tables before the definitive drain counts. Every old writer must commit or roll back before the count; installed triggers and ownership become visible in the same commit. There is no intermediate intake phase.
database_enforcement.tests: Exercise the fence against disposable PostgreSQL with competing transactions, direct application-role writes, DDL and TRUNCATE bypass attempts including CASCADE, physical and unrelated Flow fixtures, and crash/retry behavior before use on beta. A protected CI job must execute these disposable tests rather than skip them.

phases.name: fully_fenced
phases.atomicity: Under the beta deployment lock, one PostgreSQL transaction takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks on the passport job and Flow write surfaces, verifies the definitive drain and artifact-format counts, installs the durable full fence and guard ownership, then commits. In-flight work must finish before installation; no intermediate phase accepts bounded writes.
phases.drain: Require zero nonterminal passport jobs, zero legacy or unknown artifacts, zero unreadable artifacts, and zero active physical-document Flows from the identified beta database. Preserve every existing job and artifact; an unresolved row blocks installation.
phases.continuity: Wait for in-flight work before installing the fence. After installation, unrelated issuance routes and non-passport Flow writes remain available. No live Python passport signing fallback is permitted.

phases.name: rust_owner
phases.preconditions: A protected, accepted predeletion receipt and a strictly later exact-head final receipt must bind the same beta database, original fence epoch and old writer generation to the reviewed Credentials Python-passport deletion PR head. That deletion must then be merged and its replacement image built from the approved source before transition. Under the same beta deployment lock, prove the old passport-capable container has stopped and cannot be selected by the official Compose release; verify the digest-pinned replacement Credentials image has no Python passport routes and retains unrelated issuance capability for post-maintenance continuity. Bind the exact rendered aggregate service set and signed image digests, including the six Rust passport services and Gateway/Flow selectors, to the approved plan, guarded migration receipt, and read-only Rust startup validation. Keep beta passport ingress and intake closed while staged Rust services start, through the transition and until post-transition probes pass. The physical job and Flow fence must still reject valid application-role writes immediately before transition.
phases.atomicity: The privileged transition takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks on all three guarded tables in one PostgreSQL transaction, rechecks the exact fully_fenced state and original fence epoch, and repeats the frozen drain selectors: zero nonterminal jobs, legacy or unreadable artifacts, and active physical Flows; historical completed rows remain. State, guard functions and a distinct transition transaction marker change together while the original fence epoch stays immutable for receipt lineage. Until commit, every physical job and Flow write remains denied. At commit, the state becomes rust_owner and the guarded DML path becomes available to the shared application database role; source-bound process and route attestation, not SQL role identity alone, establishes the Rust generation as the sole passport owner. Preserve all job, Flow and artifact history, guard ownership, DDL and TRUNCATE denial, and unrelated issuance privileges. No temporary application-role ownership or trigger-disable window is allowed.
phases.verification: A separate rust_owner verifier must bind both the original fence epoch and distinct committed transition marker, guard definitions and grants, live beta database and container identities, exact post-deletion route selectors and signed Rust image digests. Run valid Rust-owned physical job and Flow write probes with process and route traces, plus rejection checks for removed Python passport routes and unrelated issuance continuity. Do not infer process ownership from the shared marty database role. Open beta passport ingress only after the committed state and probes pass; then record unchanged production observations and one aggregate beta deployment receipt before acceptance soak.
phases.failure: A failed or interrupted transaction remains fully_fenced. An uncertain post-commit result must be resolved by read-only inspection of the same database epoch and live service generation before any retry. After rust_owner commits, recovery is forward-only to the exact Rust release; no Python passport fallback or Rust-to-Python-to-Rust rollback is part of this wave.
phases.continuity: No Python passport owner, mixed nine-route owner or production mutation is allowed.

protected_evidence.initial: Attest source-bound beta Compose service/container/image identities, PostgreSQL system identifier and database OID, privileged guard ownership/grants, enabled trigger and function-definition hashes, the transactionally installed full fence epoch, frozen drain query/hash and zero counts, unchanged production resources, and unrelated beta service continuity. Prove a direct passport write is rejected while representative unrelated issuance writes remain possible.
protected_evidence.final: Credentials PR #305 now calls for a scoped fence, but its missing protected producer and exact-head receipts must be implemented before deletion. The producer re-inspects the same database and running shared Python container generation, proves the full fence still exists, and attests a strictly later zero-count watermark and the exact Credentials deletion PR head. A changed head or missing fence requires a new final run.
protected_evidence.rust_owner: Attest the protected receipts, post-deletion Credentials image and absent old passport-capable generation, exact rendered signed aggregate service set and Rust passport ownership, closed-then-opened beta passport ingress, exact guarded migration and transition SQL bytes, original fence epoch and separate committed transition marker, successful traced native job and physical Flow write probes, unavailable Python passport routes, unrelated issuance continuity, and unchanged production before the beta soak is accepted.
protected_evidence.absence: A deployment mutex, static Compose render, disposable database, zero-count query before the fence, or operator assertion alone is not a retirement receipt.
